primary_diagnosis_treated: Mixed diabetic‑hypertensive chronic kidney disease, stage 4
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) and NICE TA775 (SGLT2 inhibitors)

medications.purpose: Renal protection and blood pressure control in CKD with proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203: ACE‑I recommended for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension

medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive to achieve BP target <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NG203: CCB recommended as second‑line antihypertensive in CKD

medications.medication: Humulin 70/30 insulin (isophane 70 U/mL + regular 30 U/mL) as per current regimen
medications.dose: Individualised dosing based on glucose monitoring
medications.nice_justification: Diabetes management guideline (referenced in NG203 for CKD patients with diabetes)
NG203: Anaemia screening and iron replacement in CKD

medications.purpose: Slow CKD progression and reduce cardiovascular risk in eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NG203: SGLT2‑i indicated for CKD with eGFR 20‑45; TA775 supports dapagliflozin 10 mg

medications.dose: 20 mg PO once daily in the evening
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction; CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Statin recommended for all CKD patients

medications.dose: Start 20 mg PO once daily; titrate up to 80 mg BID as needed
medications.duration: Start 20 mg daily, review in 2 weeks; then ongoing as required for volume control
medications.purpose: Control volume overload and assist blood pressure control in stage 4 CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Loop diuretic may be added for fluid overload or uncontrolled hypertension

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive glucose‑lowering effect increasing risk of hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Educate patient; consider reducing rapid‑acting insulin dose by 10‑20% and monitor glucose closely after initiation

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined effect on natriuresis may cause volume depletion and acute kidney injury
interactions_checked.action: Ensure adequate hydration; check serum creatinine and potassium 1–2 weeks after starting dapagliflozin

interactions_checked.interaction: Risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury if over‑diuresed
interactions_checked.action: Start furosemide at low dose, monitor electrolytes and renal function within 1 week

interactions_checked.interaction: Both increase natriuresis → possible excessive volume loss, orthostatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Titrate furosemide cautiously; assess blood pressure and weight daily during titration

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure reading not provided – assume target <140/90 mmHg per NG203; will verify at next visit.
Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not available – assumed ≥30 mg/mmol given proteinuria label; required to confirm ACE‑I indication.
Lipid profile, liver function tests, and serum potassium not available – baseline labs needed before starting atorvastatin and to monitor after dapagliflozin/furosemide.
Serum calcium, phosphate, PTH, and bicarbonate not provided – required for CKD‑MBD assessment before adding vitamin D analogue or phosphate binder.
Full iron studies (ferritin, transferrin‑saturation) not available – to determine need for IV iron or ESA.
Allergy history not documented – will confirm no hypersensitivity to sulfonylureas, statins, or loop diuretics.
Patient’s volume status (edema, weight change) not recorded – clinical assessment needed before initiating furosemide.
treatment_summary: Continue current ACE‑I, CCB, insulin, and oral iron. Add dapagliflozin 10 mg daily and atorvastatin 20 mg nightly to address CKD progression and cardiovascular risk per NICE NG203/TA775. Introduce low‑dose furosemide 20 mg daily if fluid overload or uncontrolled hypertension is present, with careful titration. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, glucose, and blood pressure after each change, and arrange baseline labs for lipids, liver enzymes, potassium, and CKD‑MBD parameters. Review medication effectiveness and safety at 2 weeks, then at least annually.
